description.narrative:
Insatsens övergripande mål är ett samhälle där alla medborgare har möjlighet och kan agera för att utkräva ansvar. IA:s vision är en rättvis värld med starka medborgare där integritet och ansvarsutkrävande är centralt för samhällens utveckling. (A just and equitable world, where citizens are empowered and integrity is central to vibrant societies.)
IA antog en ny strategi 2018 och nuvarande strategiperiod löpte ursprungligen fram till 2023. IA hade tänkt att då övergå till en rullande strategiprocess fr o m 2022, då tanken var att årligen formulera treåriga strategiplaner som alltså naturligen kan revideras vid nästa strategiuppdatering. På detta sätt var tanken att IA skulle kunna verka mer agilt och vara snabbare i sin respons på frågor och utmaningar som uppstår. Med anledning av den starka påverkan Covid 19-pandemin visat sig ha på det civila samhället har IA beslutat sig för att snabba på övergången till rullande strategi och börja direkt. Därför kommer IA redan från 2020 att övergå till treåriga strategiplaner som revideras varje år. På så sätt får IA en strategiprocess årligen med en treårig horisont. Sida behöver formellt årligen godkänna varje ny strategi eftersom en rullande strategi per definition blir ny men det är en ganska enkel övning. Frågan är indikerad som en dialogfråga.
Strategin syftar till att uppnå tre strategiska mål: achieve, convince och amplify.
Achieve:
IA ska uppnå resultat som är hållbara och inkluderande och till gagn för medborgare. IA vill genom applikationen DevelopmentCheck skapa en återkopplingscykel som stärker hållbarhet och medborgarnas möjlighet att ta del av och påverka beslut i samhället. Man betonar särskilt vikten av att nå de mest marginaliserade. Enligt IA:s resultatramverk siktar det här målet framförallt mot att förändra människors beteenden, både rättighetsbärare och ansvarstagare. IA siktar på att påverka så att ansvarstagare och rättighetsbärare gemensamt bidrar till att åtgärda minst 50 % av de problem som rapporteras (s k fix rate).
Amplify:
IA siktar mot att bygga partnerskap för att öka, pröva och utvärdera sina aktiviteter. Genom att samarbeta med andra organisationer kan IA:s metod användas, spridas och utvecklas. Genom att testa innovationer i pilotprojekt får man idéer som sedan skalas upp, ibland med hjälp av större partner, och genererar erfarenheter i större skala som därefter systematiskt utvärderas. Detta innebär också att IA måste vara i teknologisk framkant och ha en rimlig lösning för mobilteknologi i sina verksamhetsområden.
IA avser att söka samarbeten med starkare nationella organisationer för att kunna nå skalbarhet i sina projekt. Tanken är att genom att dra lärdomar från lokal nivå kan IA se att det finns lösningar som ligger bortanför den lokala kontexten, t ex utbetalningar av lärarlöner. Genom att föra dialog om den iakttagelsen med beslutsfattare på regional eller nationell nivå hoppas IA nåbredare och även kunna påverka fler än de rättighetsbärare som är omedelbart berörda av IA:s projekt. Ett samarbete med starkare aktörer kan också vara nödvändigt när det gäller att granska tekniskt mer komplicerade projekt, så som t ex infrastruktursatsningar.
Convince:
IA:s ambition är att bevisa värdet av öppna och allmänna återkopplingsmekanismer för att inspirera andra aktörer till liknande lösningar. För att kunna göra detta kommer IA samla in evidens för fördelarna genom applikationen DevelopmentCheck, framförallt med avseende på ekonomi, miljö och sociala faktorer. Appen ska vara en naturlig rapporteringskanal för både medborgare och beslutsfattare. Man vill bygga koalitioner med andra aktörer och övertyga sådana som i sin tur har stor påverkan på andra.
Uppdaterad strategi 2021
IA uppdaterade sin strategi under 2021 och formulerar sig nu så här:
By 2023 Integrity Action will be at the forefront of demonstrating the transformational value of citizen-centred accountability to sustainable development.
Achieve
Achieve results for citizens that maximise quality, durability and inclusivity.
We will:
- Work with partners to develop evidence driven, contextualised pathways for sustained and inclusive citizen-centred accountability - Enable even the most marginalised citizens to act as monitors and benefit from monitoring - Incentivise institutions to fix at least 50% of problems identified by citizens.
Amplify
Collaborate to amplify results, fuel further innovation and embed citizen-centred accountability.
We will:
- Work with partners to sustain and scale up CCA approaches testing them as we go and evidencing results, - Take learning and insights from collaborations, feed into future R&D, and share widely to stimulate improved CCA practice globally - Be agile with tech developments to ensure the efficiency, accessibility and local adoption of tools.
Convince
Build a robust case for citizen-centred accountability to inspire its mainstreaming
- Lead on evidencing the economic, environmental and social case for citizen-centred accountability - Build or support coalitions to call for the mainstreaming of citizen-centred accountability at the global level and within countries - Convince influencers and institutions to demand citizen-centred accountability.

Integrity Action har ansökt om stöd från Sida om 28 MSEK för att genomföra sin globala strategi "Ambition for open citizen feedback" under perioden 1 oktober 2020 - 30 september 2024
Insatsen syftar till att bidra till samhällen där alla medborgare har möjlighet och också utkräver ansvar av de ansvarstagare medborgarna förlitar sig på. Detta görs genom att arbeta med tre målområden: 1) uppnå, 2) förstärka, och 3) övertyga. Integrity Action vill uppnå direkta resultat för medborgarna i form av förbättrad samhällsservice (uppnå). Genom att sprida sin metod hoppas Integrity Action kunna få andra organisationer att anta en liknande ansats till gagn för ännu fler människor (amplify). Integrity Action avser att hela tiden samla in kunskap om hur metoden fungerar för att kunna stärka argumentet och bidra till att andra aktörer använder samma metod (övertyga).
Insatsens totala budget för programperioden är 105 MSEK.

Integrity Action has applied to Sida for funding of 28 MSEK to carry out its global strategy "Ambition for open citizen feedback" during the period 1 October 2020 - 30 September 2024.
The intervention aims at helping build “societies in which all citizens can – and do – successfully demand integrity from the institutions they rely on”. To realise this goal, Integrity Action has identified three objectives or focus areas: 1) achieve, 2) amplify, and 3) convince. Integrity Action intends to reach direct positive results for citizens (achieve). By working with other organisations, Integrity Action hopes to spread its methodology and make other actors adopt a similar approach which would benefit even more rights-holders (amplify). Integrity Action plans to build evidence that proves the impact of its approach and use this knowledge to generate further amplifying partnerships (convince).
The interventions total budget for the program period is 105 MSEK.

title.narrative: Amendment to the Agreement Integrity Action 2022

description.narrative:
Example of results achieved presented by Integrity Action in the Annual Report for 2024-25
N.B. IA wrote in their report: "It is worth noting that this workplan (Sida addition: meaning the RAF that was submitted to Sida) was developed and submitted while Integrity Action was still with Crown Agents and had no information on the future folding of the organisation. Targets, therefore, were informed by the understanding that our merger with Crown Agents would have brought scale. This means that some targets were, unfortunately not met."
Achieve: Objective 1, Achieve results for citizens that maximise quality, durability and inclusivity
Sida notes that Integrity Action themselves state the following regarding Objective 1 Achieve (the annex report to Sida, p.3): "Wherever we implement programmes, we witness positive outcomes and impact. In addition to that, the way we design and implement programmes is highly ethical and based on our justice approach. The evaluation of Integrity Clubs and the Children Resilience Fund provide us with evidence; in addition to this, anecdotal and informal feedback have also backed the quality and impact of our programming. However, the scale of our programmes is still too small to test other assumptions."
Sida understands the situation and why this is happening. Sida agrees with the analysis above that the scale of IA's programmes is still too small. Sida will expect more positive results for the final year (July25-June 2026).
Sida notes that IA have had operations in Ukraine, Kenya and South Africa during the operational year. There has also been a Green Accountability accelerator pilot for citizen centered accountability (the CCA model) in green sector during 6 months. All, but Ukraine, are still rather small-scale projects though. When asked, IA says there were only 30 monitors active in the year.. See below.
One example of an activity under Objective 1: Implement IA's newly-developed model for citizen monitoring of carbon markets in at least one initiative" Status by IA: A pilot was ready in Nigeria, but due to licencing delays caused by standar issuer Verra, it hasn't started yet. We have engaged stakeholders in looking for the alternative sites." This example is somewhat illustrating for how the operations have been under Objective 1.
Sida asked follow-up questions in the Annual Review Meeting in March 2026, regarding the actual figures.
* The actual number of monitors monitoring for FY25 was 30 people and that they were all located in South Africa. A refresher training was held in February 2025 for these monitors. Sida: Sida notes that this is much less than previous year, when there were in fact a few hundred monitors active. This is a a not sufficient result according to Sida, but again Sida knows the background to it.
* The number of beneficiaries under the Children Resilience Fund in Ukraine was 17 Civil Society Organisations and 74,207 individuals, of which more than 50,000 were children. Sida: This was a positive result to hear and that IA indirectly (via Ukrainian CSO partners) were able to reach so many rights-holders. Sida: This is a very positive outcome and a good example of working with support the local CSOs that in their turn can support more rights-holders and in a better way.
Reflection: Sida notes that IA has struggled during this operational year too, to fulfill mainly their objectives in their own ongoing programmes (that is Objective 1. Achieve.) The main reasons according to the reporting, were that IA managed to attract new funding, but that those projects could not yet be follow-up and measured as they fell outside of the project timeline. For example indicator 1a in the RAF where IA set up to follow the percentage of surveyed monitors who believed that they can make a difference to their local projects. This could not be done.
Sida expects that those projects will be possible to measure adequately and that report on in the final year (July25-June 2026) incoming to Sida in October 2026, will show these positive results.
Amplify: Objective 2, Collaborate to amplify results, fuel further innovation and embed citizen-centred accountability
Sida concludes that IA has been successful during the year when it comes to continuing to diversify their funding. They aimed for securing 6 donors and managed to achieve 4 donors, which is assessed by Sida as a good result. IA aimed to achieve 4 million GBP and reached 3,4 million GBP, which must also be viewed as a satisfying result. Sida agrees with IA that they have successfully built on the relationships and visibility obtained during IA's short time with Crown Agents.
Sida also notes that they have made progress regarding number of partners/ duty-bearers actively engaged in Integrity Action programmes who were inspired to sustain or scale up citizen-centered accountability (CCA) mechanisms. They aimed for 2 and achieved 7 (for instance. For instance their two partner organisations (PARI and SALGA) in South Africa that are now seeking funding on their own to continue the methods. See indicator 2c in RAF for more details)
Objective 2 was (as the other two objectives) planned when IA was part of Crown Agents, but despite the folding of Crown Agent, Sida assesses IA has manged to achieve a lot of positive output.
Sida assesses that Objective 2 is the most successful objective out of the three objectives.
Accelerate: Objective 3, Build and share a robust case for CCA to catalyse its effective mainstreaming
Sida notes that IA has made some progress in sharing their model with other organisations and operations. IA aimed for external policies and practices to influenced or informed by Integrity Action's programming, research, or insights. IA reports that there are strong examples with FCDO and the Ministry of Education in Philippines. FCDO is planning to include CCA in some their operations and if they do, this could open a lot of interesting possibilities for IA and their partners. The Government of the Philippines is interested in embedding the Integrity Clubs model and is actively trying to include into national policy before deploying it.
IA mentions in their report that they designed and commissioned two pieces of learning (External evaluation of Children Resilience Fund (CRF) and learning on sustainability and impact of Integrity Clubs). This was part of their goal to design and commission at least two new pieces of research to enhance the case for citizen-centred accountability (CCA).
Overall Sida assesses that some of the goals under Objective 3 have been met, but that the results are not very satisfying. However, it is in line with what Sida expected based on the information that Sida has received during the last year.
Finally regarding the results achieved: Sida noted there is little analysis and reflection made by IA on their achieved results during the year and therefore Sida asked IA in the Annual Review Meeting March 2026 to reflect on their achievements. IA replied: "IA is proud of the resilience and adaptation found in these turbulent years and therefore reflects positively on the organisations achievements. IA is finding new ways to evolve to maintain its place in the third sector against shrinking civil space at home and abroad."
Conclusion: Overall the achieved results are slightly better than in last year's (July 2023-June 2024) reporting (except for Objective 1), but the results are not sufficient according to Sida.
Overall Sida maintains our conclusion drawn a year ago, that IA's operations are too small, not geographically spread and /or within more operative organisations and that the scaling up is still taking a long time to achieve.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
